Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely praised crime‑thrillers released in 2020 (and even late 2019 releases that were still fresh in 2020):

| Film | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| **The Invisible Man** (2017) – *Re‑released in 2020* | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that blends sci‑fi with domestic abuse tropes; it was re‑released in 2020 due to its strong word‑of‑mouth buzz. |
| **Tenet** (2020) | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson | Nolan’s mind‑bending time‑travel heist film; praised for its ambition and action choreography. |
| **The Gentlemen** (2019) – *Re‑released in 2020* | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced, witty gangster caper; gained cult status after streaming release. |
| **Uncut Gems** (2019) – *Streaming in 2020* | Ben Safdie & Joshua Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett | A tense, high‑octane look at New York's underground gambling scene; Sandler’s performance is a standout. |
| **The Irishman** (2019) – *Netflix binge in 2020* | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Scorsese’s epic mob saga; the film’s long runtime and deep character study made it a talking point throughout 2020. |
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** (2020) | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that mixes historical events with sharp dialogue; Sorkin’s script won an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay. |
| **Mank** (2020) | David Fincher | Gary Oldman, Amanda Seyfried | Fincher’s black‑and‑white homage to Hollywood’s golden age; it offers a meta‑look at screenwriting and studio politics. |
| **The Hunt** (2020) | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish thriller that follows a man falsely accused of child abuse; it’s intense, claustrophobic, and socially relevant. |
| **The Night House** (2020) | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Lane | A psychological horror‑thriller that doubles as a crime mystery; Hall’s performance earned her an Oscar nomination. |

### How to Watch Them
- **Streaming Platforms:** Many of these films found new life on Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, or Hulu during 2020. Check your local listings or use “JustWatch” to see where each title is available in your region.
- **Home Media:** If you prefer physical copies, several titles were released on Blu‑ray/DVD in early 2021, often with director commentaries and behind‑the‑scenes extras.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more details on any particular movie—like cast bios, critical reception, or where to stream them!
